summary: In major military space developments, a U.S. intelligence report revealed that Russia is developing a nuclear space weapon, while United Launch Alliance’s latest launch failure has created operational challenges for the U.S. Space Force. Concurrently, the U.S. Air Force awarded a $16 billion engine work contract to dozens of companies, even as the Department of the Air Force failed its financial audit. In civil exploration, NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter temporarily halted science operations on Mars due to technical glitches, though the Curiosity rover successfully collected new surface samples and observed drifting twilight clouds. Internationally, engine trouble forced Japan’s Hayabusa2 probe to alter its mission plans and cancel a planned asteroid landing, while the European Space Agency's Hera probe inspected NASA's previous asteroid crash site. In commercial tech and science news, RBC Signals raised $10 million to commercialize new communication systems, NASA issued new seed funding for small business innovation, researchers devised a new method to extract oxygen from lunar soil, and scientists verified the first captured image of a black hole. Looking ahead, observers should watch for the upcoming launch of China’s rocket carrying the first international astronaut to the Tiangong space station following its recent rollout to the pad.
